To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the combination of stereovision and LIDAR is a good approach to detect and track objects at long range.

the proposed system is able to detect obstacles at a range of 50 meters, that it can detect obstacles with a size as small as 10cm, that it can be implemented on a real-time platform (at 15Hz), that it is able to detect moving obstacles and that it has a very low false detection rate (less than 1 false detection per 10 seconds of driving).
the proposed fusion method is able to detect and to track obstacles with a detection rate of about 90% and a false detection rate of 0% in a range of about 100m.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a generic obstacle detection system for driving assistance, based on laser scanner and stereovision.
the development of a long range obstacle detection system based upon the fusion of two sensors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in our experiments, the best results are obtained with the fusion between the stereovision and the laser detection.
the best algorithm is the one which is able to take advantage of the strengths of the two sensors.
the fusion of the two methods is efficient and robust for long range obstacle detection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a generic road obstacle detection method based on fusion between a laser scanner and a stereovision system.
stereovision is a good tool for the confirmation of laser detections.
stereovision is not a good solution for long range road obstacle detection but can be used to confirm the laser detections.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fusion of stereovision and LRF can improve the detection rate and the false detection rate.
a good detection rate can be obtained with a low false alarm rate.
the combination between the laser scanner and the stereovision can be used to detect and track road obstacles in a long range, and with an extremely low false alarm rate.
